I would keep my land in the pattern I know best. On my 19.1 mu, I would put 15.0 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and keep 4.1 mu in cotton. I have 30 years of experience, only three people in the household, and I can irrigate from a well, so I would choose a plan that is steady, familiar, and not too labor-heavy. For wheat and maize, I would use better seed because those are my main grain crops and I want stable yield from the irrigated land. For cotton, I would also use better seed, but I would keep the area smaller because cotton takes more management and more spraying. I would use moderate fertilizer, not extreme rates, because I would rather protect yield stability and control costs. I would irrigate wheat more than cotton, and maize enough to get through key growth stages. I would use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, my labor situation, and the way I would prepare land efficiently at the start of the season.
